A notebook, not a collection of disconnected tools
A complete screen map, plain-language feature glossary, practical walkthrough and proposed interaction specification. Landscape slides are designed for presentation or comfortable zooming.

CURRENT = available in published 0.12, not a promise that every device behaves identically. PROPOSED = requested redesign, not yet shipped. VALIDATE = a behaviour that must be checked in the replacement build.
The wireframes are real vector layouts, not screenshots of a finished build. An SVG companion can be imported into Figma. This is not a hosted Figma file or a claimed Figma prototype.
Notes, Archive and Trash are library destinations. Folders and labels organise notes. Search, filters, view and sort change how you find or see them.
A note = the document you work in
Text or a checklist is the main content. Images, drawings and diagrams are visual content. A reminder is a scheduled property of a note, not a kind of drawing or a separate notebook.
Read image extracts text from a picture. Record voice captures audio and may produce a transcript. Voice inbox holds originals. Settings, Storage & recovery, Backups and About are app-level services.
Drawing: ink and simple geometric marks made on a canvas. Image: a photo or imported picture. Diagram: separately editable shapes and connectors, such as a flowchart.
Reminder: a date and time attached to a note. Archive: keep a note out of the active list without deleting it. Trash: deleted notes awaiting recovery or permanent deletion.
Library: the collection and its destinations. Folder: a note location, reflected under the chosen main storage path when configured. Label: a reusable tag; a note can have several.
Open Notes. Choose New text note or Checklist. Add a useful title and content. Use Back to return to the library; normal edits are saved automatically.
A save or storage warning matters. Automatic saving is not a reason to ignore a failed destination update. Private recovery and the selected folder can have different states.
Search a distinctive word. If the note is missing, clear labels/filters, check the selected folder and look in Archive or Trash before assuming deletion.
Search, open a note, create a text note or checklist. A pinned note is visually marked with a filled pin. Opening Library should reveal clear destinations, not a second confusing toolbar.
Choose notes using visible selection controls; arbitrary combinations are allowed. Selection mode should show a count and the available bulk actions. Cancel selection without changing notes.
The Library swipe begins inside the left portion of the screen, rather than the system Back edge. The visible Library control remains available; a gesture must never be the only route.
A lens on the library, not another storage location
Choose list or grid. This changes presentation, not note contents or folder paths. Keep this separate from selection mode and content editing.
Order by created or edited time. A sort option is not a label and does not move a note into another folder. The active choice should remain visibly selected.
Select any useful combination of labels. Show active filters and a clear reset path. A filtered empty result must say that it is filtered, not imply the entire library is empty.
Choose the main local folder in Storage & recovery. Create a named folder, then move selected notes into it. Verify the folder and readable note filenames in the Android file manager.
Open Labels on a note, choose or create labels, then return to the library and filter by a label. Several labels can describe one note without making extra note copies.
A folder move is a file operation, not just a renamed chip. Report a failed move and retained source honestly. Filenames use a useful note prefix and timestamp rather than opaque random names.
The document, its content and its properties
Back, pin, archive and contextual undo belong to the note. Note-level Copy and Trash belong to library/list actions; native copying of selected text remains available in the editor.
Title and text/checklist first. Visual items follow in clearly separated cards. A reminder chip is a property near the note header, not a miscellaneous image attachment.
Add opens content/capture choices. Text formatting applies to text. Colour/background and labels organise appearance and classification. More holds less-frequent actions, not essential editing.
Use native Android caret movement and precise text selection. Select words or ranges, then apply formatting. The selected-text Copy action is different from copying a whole note.
Bold, italic, underline, strike and headings should act on an understandable range. Larger headings must reflow following paragraphs rather than overlap them.
Create items, check them, change indentation and reorder using the available item controls. Hide checked items only when wanted. Conversion to or from text is an explicit operation.
Image adds an existing picture. Drawing opens an ink canvas. Diagram opens structured shapes and connectors. These should be separately named and separately recognisable.
Read image extracts words from a picture; it is not the same as attaching that picture. Record voice captures an original recording and attempts offline transcription.
Reminder opens date and time selection for this note. It belongs in Add as requested, then appears as a distinct, tappable reminder chip in the note.
Stop treating every visual item as the same image
Every card has a type badge, preview and compact action strip. Use Drawing, Image or Diagram as the primary type. Show a filename or caption only when useful, not as a second competing heading.
Use an edit icon with a specific accessible name, and a secondary More menu for removal and related actions. Do not place tall, full-width Edit drawing / Remove image text rows under every preview.

Remove drawing, Remove image and Remove diagram must describe the actual content. Removal is not deletion of the entire note. Destructive actions need a clear target and a recovery/confirmation policy.
Why the supplied screen feels unfinished
The landscape white paper sits inside a tall dark page, leaving large empty regions. The selected tool looks like plain text. Save is a text button and delete competes with frequent controls.
Let the workspace use the available screen between compact top and bottom controls. Give tools real selection states, icons and names. Remove the persistent gesture paragraph.
The redesign must work for portrait, landscape and larger text. Canvas coordinates and exports must not stretch. Existing saved drawings and drafts must remain readable.

Back and Drawing on the left. Save icon immediately before the top-right three-dot menu. Save attaches or updates the drawing in the original note; Back retains the draft without pretending it was attached.
A horizontal tool strip: Pen, Pencil, Highlighter, Eraser, Line, Rectangle, Oval. Each has an icon and short label. The selected tool has a filled accent surface and selected accessibility state.
Ink colour, stroke width, Undo, Redo and Fit occupy a compact dock. Large-font or narrow screens can scroll the tool strip; targets remain at least 48 dp. No persistent instruction paragraph.
Three dots hold options, not the main workflow

An explicit checked toggle shows or hides a workspace grid. Grid lines are a guide, not drawing content: they must not appear in saved images or copied images unless a future explicit export option says so.
Copy the rendered drawing image, not a screenshot of the app. Android clipboard receives a readable PNG URI with a proper content type and grant. Say Copied only after the image is available.

Delete or clear must identify its scope: clear this canvas versus remove this attached drawing from the note. Keep destructive options in More and confirm them; preserve draft/Undo behaviour where applicable.
From the first stroke to a reusable picture

Open Add > Drawing. Choose a visibly selected tool; choose ink and width in the lower dock. Draw in the canvas. Pinch and two-finger navigation can remain supported without occupying a permanent text paragraph.
Switch tools, Undo or Redo. Use Fit to recover the view. Use Grid lines from More when alignment helps. The guide must not change the exported artwork.
Use the top Save icon to attach/update the drawing. Copy as image is independent of Save and must not silently edit the note. Return to the note and see a Drawing card with a compact edit action.
Add > Image opens the Android picker. Select a supported local picture. The note gets an Image card. This operation preserves the note if decoding, size checks or the picker fails.
Add > Read image starts offline OCR. Choose the available language, select an image, process it and review the recognised text. OCR can make mistakes; it does not certify the image text as correct.
An imported photo is not a Drawing. OCR output is editable text, not a Diagram. Do not label all three with the same generic image removal wording or claim OCR attaches the original automatically.
Structured visual thinking, not freehand ink
A flowchart or structured sketch made from separate shapes and connectors. Each shape has a type, label, position and size. Unlike a flattened drawing, its elements remain individually editable.
Choose among the supported shape types, select a shape, edit its label/colour, move it, connect it and use Undo/Redo. Grouping and arrow editing have distinct controls.

Tap a shape to show resize handles at the appropriate corners or fixed points. Drag a handle for a live size preview, then release to commit one undoable change. Remove Wider/Narrower/Taller/Shorter from the normal menu.
Show a clear outline and reachable handles. A first tap selects; a drag inside moves. A drag beginning on a handle resizes. Connector endpoints must not be mistaken for resize handles.
Rectangles and ellipses use bounds handles; diamonds use the meaningful bounds/vertices. Keep minimum sizes and readable labels. Do not invert a shape or silently drag it off the document.

Handle hit targets remain screen-sized when the display changes. Convert pointer positions through the viewport scale. Resizing grouped shapes, moving connectors, rotated displays and Undo need explicit tests before acceptance.
A schedule attached to a note
Open a note, choose Add > Reminder, then choose date and time. A distinct reminder chip shows the scheduled time. Tap the chip to edit; a clear action removes the schedule without deleting content.
Notification permission and device power/background policies affect delivery. Permission denial must leave normal note editing usable. Check notification settings if a reminder did not alert.
Use Reminder, not remainder. Reminder is a note property and an app notification workflow, not an attachment. Rich recurrence/calendar functionality is not claimed as fully delivered.
Editable words plus a retained original
Record voice is optional and contextual; microphone denial must not block text notes. Stop recording to retain the audio before offline recognition is attempted.
Voice inbox is a library destination for originals. Cards show playback progress and play/pause controls; seeking should be understandable. Export WAV and retry transcript are secondary actions.
Review recognition and conservative punctuation. Failure of an offline model must not erase the original audio. Technical engine/model information belongs in About, not the primary capture controls.
Mark a note as important without moving or duplicating it. The selected pin is filled, and its accessible name should change to Unpin.
Remove a note from the active Notes view while retaining it in Archive. Unarchive returns it to active notes; this is not recovery from deletion.

Deleted notes can be restored or permanently deleted. Automatic expiry is seven days; manual permanent deletion and emptying Trash are also available. Explain permanence and never purge live note files by mistake.
Consistent signature, not a stock-looking island
System follows the device appearance. Light and Dark are explicit app choices. Embedded MySpace hosts own their appearance policy under the host contract.
Replace the visually disconnected default radio dialog shown in your screenshot with a signature sheet: three clearly selected cards, matching surfaces, rounded geometry and readable contrast.
Use the same sheet/menu language for tools, colours, widths and confirmations. Platform file pickers and permission prompts remain Android-owned; do not disguise them as app-designed screens.
Appearance of a note, not its location
Choose a note colour for recognition. Colour must remain readable in both light and dark themes. It is not a label, folder or reminder priority.
Background options are a separate visual property, including the available coloured tints. Preserve content and precise text selection when changing backgrounds.
Show the active swatch with more than colour alone: an outline or check, plus a readable accessible name. Do not rely on a user remembering which similarly coloured dot they tapped.
Appearance and Home widget. Widget placement is initiated by Android and may differ by launcher. Users can remove and re-add widgets without deleting notes.
Storage & recovery and Backups. Show current destination and any pending save clearly. Keep advanced recovery choices below the normal choose-folder/retry actions.
Diagnostics is opt-in troubleshooting. About contains version, offline model information and licences. It should not compete visually with everyday writing controls.
Know where your notes are safe

Use device storage or select a main local folder. Folder selection goes through the Android picker and needs useful read/write permission. Local file names and physical subfolders should reflect actual operations.
A private recovery copy and a successful external save are not the same claim. If the folder is unavailable or revoked, show the pending state and Retry save rather than silently claiming completion.
Do not clear app data or uninstall to solve a storage warning before exporting/verifying a backup. Opening an existing library requires validation and an understandable merge preview.
A portable copy is not automatic cloud sync
The published JSON backup preserves supported note data, including embedded images. It does not contain original voice recordings. Export originals separately from Voice inbox when needed.
Pick a local backup, validate it, review added/identical/conflicting notes and confirm. Changed-ID conflicts are preserved as copies; a previous-state checkpoint is written.

Audio-inclusive ZIP staging, validation and conflict-planning foundations exist in development. They are not an end-user feature yet. This request takes priority; no archive UI or complete transactional restore is claimed.
A selected-text copy uses Android text selection. Whole-note copy is a library/list action. Sharing text does not create a complete backup of drawings, originals or app state.
PDF is for reading/presentation, including supported diagram output. A readable PDF is not a restorable editable note backup. Success requires valid output, not just a created zero-byte filename.
Copy as image supplies a PNG through Android clipboard. Pasting depends on the receiving app supporting image clips; a text-only destination cannot be promised to accept it.
Find a note without losing your place
Create Project planning, assign a project folder, add a Work label and pin it while active. Put a diagram in the note when its content needs a flowchart.
Search a word, then choose the relevant folder or labels and your preferred view/sort. Make active constraints visible so you know why other notes are absent.
Unpin and archive the note when complete. Use Trash only when deletion is intended. Recovery belongs in Trash or Backups, not in View or Sort.
One document, several clearly divided components
Write observations as text or checklist items. Attach a photo as Image. Use Read image if you need words extracted. Add a Drawing for annotations and a Diagram for the process flow.
Keep title and properties at the top, main writing next and typed content cards after it. Use consistent spacing and a small type badge; show actions only beside their own content.
Add a Reminder to the note. If voice is useful, record it and retain the original in Voice inbox. None of these actions should create an unexplained stack of generic image controls.
Compact does not mean tiny or cryptic

Frequently repeated actions can be icons, but every icon needs a specific accessible label and long-press help. Drawing tools keep both icon and text as requested; essential state must be visibly selected.
Keep 48 dp hit targets, scrollable tool rows and reachable actions. Test portrait, landscape, tablet and 200% text. Do not use smaller text simply to fit a crowded toolbar.
No permanent explanatory paragraph crowding the canvas. Put optional gesture help in More. Do not sacrifice native text selection, contrast or Back behaviour to match a mockup.
What must be checked before calling this finished

Full available workspace; distinct selected tool chips; two compact rows; top Save and More; working grid toggle; real PNG clipboard; scoped deletion; correct Drawing/Image labels and no stale draft loss.
Direct handles replace size command buttons. Test supported geometry, connector attachment, cancellation and Undo. Review signature sheets in light/dark, large font and narrow layouts.
New native tests, rendered screen review and real-device retest are separate evidence. An authored test is not a passing test; a passing emulator is not acceptance on the Motorola Android 16 device.
This document is the first deliverable, not a completion claim

App vocabulary and categories documented. Detailed screen and feature walkthrough supplied. Requested drawing, attachment, appearance and diagram changes specified as proposals. Vector PDF/SVG handoff supplied.

Find: Search. Change list/grid/order: Filter & view. Move location: Folders. Tag: Labels. Keep out of active list: Archive. Recover deletion: Trash. Recover a library: Backups/Storage & recovery.
Write: Text/Checklist. Add a photo: Image. Ink: Drawing. Editable flowchart: Diagram. Extract words from a photo: Read image. Capture speech: Record voice; originals live in Voice inbox.

Schedule: Reminder in Add, then its note chip. Note appearance: Colour/Background. App appearance: Settings > Appearance. File destination: Storage & recovery. Troubleshoot: Diagnostics. Version/models: About.

Pen draws a solid stroke. Pencil uses a lighter, finer stroke. Highlighter lays a broader translucent stroke so underlying marks remain visible. Ink colour and stroke width affect new strokes, not all previous marks.

Eraser paints white over the raster drawing; it is not object selection. Line makes one straight segment. Rectangle and Oval create outlines, not filled blocks. Drag from one extent of the shape to the other.

Undo/Redo act on this editing session. Fit resets the view, not the artwork. Grid is a visual guide, not artwork. Older drawings reopen as pixels; individual historical strokes are not promised to remain editable after reopening.

Rectangle: a process or activity. Diamond: a decision. Capsule: start/end. Parallelogram: input/output. Oval: an alternative start/end or general shape. Text annotation adds a label without a process box.

Triangle, Right triangle, Pentagon, Hexagon, Octagon, Star, Trapezoid, Cylinder, Cube, Wavy rectangle, Cloud, Right arrow, Chevron, Semicircle and Heart. Shape labels and connectors supply your meaning; geometry is not automatic flowchart validation.

An arrow links two shapes and can have a label such as Yes/No. A group moves related shapes together. Selecting a shape is not selecting its whole text or copying its pixels. Resize handles adjust its bounds, not the note font.
Useful limits to know before a large import

Published note images: up to eight per note. Imported image streams are bounded to 20 MiB, normalised to a maximum 1600 px edge and a bounded encoded payload. The complete JSON library/backup safety boundary is 8 MiB.

Read image uses bundled English, Hindi/Devanagari and Kannada OCR. The bundled speech recogniser is the small English model; it is not a promise of equivalent Hindi/Kannada speech support or universal accent accuracy.

Arbitrary file attachments, rich recurring reminders, complete widgets, wall drag ordering, universal providers and audio-inclusive backup restoration are not all completed. No login/cloud sync is required for normal local notes. A detailed guide must not invent missing features.
Know what happened, not just what button you pressed
The image or drawing is missing

Check the original note, attachment limit and library-size warning. An unsuccessful image operation must leave the existing note unchanged. A retained drawing draft is not the same as a saved attachment.
The file exists but may be unusable

A zero-byte filename is not a successful PDF or backup. Export should report a verified result only after checking the output. Local provider restrictions are intentional; choose Internal storage or SD card rather than a cloud destination.

Diagnostics are optional local app-event logs, not a screen recording. They omit note bodies/audio/images and intentionally hide notice content. Lack of a crash/error record does not prove the UI worked well. Review any export before sharing.

A tall retained page opens at full width instead of fitting into a narrow strip. Two fingers pan through the page. Artwork is retained in the complete exported image; the viewport is not the export boundary.

Fit shows the whole page and can intentionally leave margins when page and window differ. It must not modify artwork or undo history. This last refinement is source-only, not a captured Android success.
Start portrait, add ink low on the page, rotate to a wide viewport and draw near the right edge. Verify both strokes in export. Fit should show the overview without changing exported pixels.
